Single enrollment uses a random 32-byte secret, stores only SHA-256 plus a 5-minute expiry, binds origin, and returns the token inside the command (internal/cluster/light_service.go:76-118); enrollment verifies origin/token/expiry and atomically consumes the matching hash while saving host data (light_service.go:129-172; light_store.go:255-276,279-354). Batch enrollment intentionally permits maxUses 1..MaxHosts with 5-minute..7-day expiry and persisted attempt identity (light_batch_service.go:27-98,120-204; cmd/kejilion-node/main.go:175-205; batch_enrollment_attempt.go:24-75,78-127). Windows installation accepts only install --stdin, checks elevation, bounds input to 8 KiB, checks the protected executable path and signature, writes a SystemOnly handoff, and starts bootstrap; bootstrap requires SYSTEM, reads/removes the handoff immediately, clears its buffer, verifies binaries, then calls enrollment in-process and clears request.Token (cmd/kejilion-node/service_windows.go:83-167,169-225,227-250). ProgramData/Program Files roots and SystemOnly explicit descriptor/atomic writes are source-defined (internal/windowsnode/paths_windows.go:20-31; security_windows.go:46-79,310-382); node config persists EnrollmentTokenHash instead of the raw enrollment token (main.go:253-260; platform_windows.go:165-184). local_checks.invariant: A one-time enrollment capability should not become available to an unauthorized principal through the one-line administrator PowerShell command, shell history, or logging before its intended expiry and use limit.
local_checks.result: Source trace: the command creation endpoint requires Origin, session and CSRF; audit events include expiry/protocol metadata but not the returned command (internal/panel/cluster.go:370-408,1029-1037). The Windows command passes Token as a reversible Base64-decoding PowerShell expression (internal/cluster/light_windows_install.go:12-16,62); Base64 is not secrecy. The installer explicitly tells operators to review PSReadLine history and revoke unused batch tokens (deploy/windows/install.ps1:155). A single token expires in five minutes; batch tokens have bounded expiry and max-use count (internal/cluster/light_service.go:95-118; light_batch_service.go:17-22,48-78). The source proves a credential-bearing command is presented to an interactive elevated shell and that history/logging is a recognized exposure class; it does not prove the history is persisted, accessible to a lower-trust principal, collected centrally, or exploitable before token consumption/expiry. No leakage is asserted.

local_checks.invariant: A lower-trust local principal must not be able to recover and redeem a still-valid one-time Windows node enrollment token from the administrator's PowerShell history or another local copy.
local_checks.result: The source supports a conditional exposure path but does not prove the required lower-trust read. The panel endpoint returns the generated command to a session-authenticated, Origin- and CSRF-checked caller, and the UI renders/copies it. The Windows command embeds the token in a PowerShell expression that reversibly Base64-decodes it; this is encoding, not encryption. install.ps1 explicitly warns the operator to review PSReadLine history for enrollment tokens. However, repository source does not establish the target machine's PSReadLine history location, history mode, file ownership/DACL, or that a non-admin principal can read any historical copy. I therefore cannot confirm a cross-principal exposure from source alone and do not infer machine ACLs or logging behavior. Candidate remains needs_validation because lower-trust local read/access and the deployment redemption route were not established; no leakage is asserted. unresolved: The effective PSReadLine history behavior/profile ACL, script-block or endpoint logging collection/retention, execution mode, and whether a lower-trust principal can recover the reversible token are not source-observable. Do not infer leakage from the warning.

local_checks.invariant: A signed Windows node report must be bound to its enrolled node identity and reject reuse of an authenticated request before it refreshes center telemetry state.
local_checks.result: Server-side identity checks are present: report HMAC covers POST, endpoint path, node ID, timestamp, request ID, and SHA-256 of the raw body; the center loads the enrolled node secret, checks a two-minute timestamp window, and compares signatures in constant time (internal/cluster/light_service.go:47-61,276-303). The report endpoint supplies those values from headers and passes the exact bounded body (internal/panel/cluster.go:935-963). A possible replay gap remains across Service reconstruction: the report calls s.replays.Accept(nodeID, requestID), while each Service initializes a new replayGuard and replayGuard stores only an in-memory map (internal/cluster/light_service.go:186-229; internal/cluster/service.go:308; internal/cluster/guard.go:8-44). After acceptance, UpdateReport stamps ReceivedAt, LastAttemptAt, and LastSuccessAt with now and replaces LastSnapshot (internal/cluster/light_store.go:489-521). Incremental diff recheck against comparison_base 4c0694aa8e02e46145a775707b8d5a0355f7ce10 (run-metadata.json and coverage-check.json): AcceptLightReport HMAC authentication, the replay call, the in-memory guard construction, and UpdateReport freshness writes are unchanged generic code. The increment adds Windows platform enrollment/recording and Windows report-platform validation, so the existing replay/reset behavior newly applies to the newly supported Windows report surface; the candidate is limited to that scope expansion and does not claim a newly introduced replay primitive. The report route itself pre-existed.

local_checks.invariant: A previously accepted signed light-node report should not be accepted again as a fresh report by a lower-trust principal after Service reconstruction while its authenticated timestamp remains valid; replayed Windows metadata must not receive a fresh capability timestamp without a current authenticated node report.
local_checks.result: Source proves a process-local replay guard reset on NewService reconstruction and a concrete accepted replay window: the same complete request can pass again while its HMAC timestamp remains within plus or minus two minutes, if the caller already has that valid request. Acceptance stamps ReceivedAt with current server time, then UpdateReport replaces LastSnapshot, sets LastSuccessAt, clears failure state, and marks the store dirty. For Windows records, the new platform/capability metadata uses ReceivedAt for a 90-second capability freshness decision. The generic replay guard and light report replay check existed in the comparison base; they are not new primitives in this run. The changed Windows applicability adds platform/capability metadata to the already guarded report flow. Source does not establish that a principal lower-trust than the authorized node reporter can obtain the complete valid request or key. No arbitrary terminal/file control or data disclosure follows from the report HMAC alone because those controls use separate Noise identities. Keep this as needs_validation pending the exact deployed transcript-access fact; do not infer passive TLS capture. Independent comparison-base source checks show the same in-memory replay guard, report HMAC, replay call and ReceivedAt update existed at comparison_base; Windows telemetry/capability is the new applicability. This is not evidence that a lower-trust actor can obtain a valid complete signed request.

unresolved: The source proves process-local replay state and a two-minute signed-timestamp acceptance window, but this source-only pass did not establish whether an attacker can obtain a complete authenticated report in the deployed network path or whether deployed restart behavior preserves the same Service instance.

The ledger starting paths do not include the Windows report sender/key-storage implementation, so client-side request-ID generation, retry behavior, and local reporting-key protection remain unreviewed.

No runtime evidence was collected; impact is bounded to replay of a captured valid request inside its signed timestamp window, potentially refreshing the existing host snapshot/freshness. This does not establish identity forgery without a valid signature or credential.

excluded_blocks.reason: Carry prior fingerprint terminal-sse-output-after-session-revocation; recheck its current source trace, but do not decide browser receipt or the required logout timing without bounded isolation and owner contract.

local_checks.invariant: Only the authenticated browser session that owns a terminal may receive its output; logout/session deletion must stop future SSE output according to the documented revocation timing.
local_checks.result: Source trace: panel routes GET /api/v1/terminal-stream and the subscriptions endpoint to handleTerminalStream; opening requires requireSession, and the stream is bound to both user ID and hash of the session token. Subscription changes require POST plus Origin/CSRF and lookup requires the same user and token hash; terminal subscriptions also require the Panel terminal session owner to match the user (internal/panel/server.go:462-463; internal/panel/terminal_stream.go:170-191,265-345). Logout requires Origin/CSRF then auth.Logout -> Store.DeleteSession; Authenticate resolves the token against SessionByTokenHash, so a later stream recheck sees deletion (internal/panel/server.go:1055-1072; internal/auth/service.go:577-610; internal/store/store.go:704-733). Password/credential transitions also revoke stored user sessions in the Store. Output pumps obtain backend output for the Panel session owner and enqueue it; the SSE writer checks the session on each event/heartbeat, caches successful authentication for no more than one second, writes auth.expired on failure, and short-circuits before writing the dequeued event (internal/panel/terminal_stream.go:233-264,365-426; internal/panel/terminal.go:195-250,290-355,436-440). Session expiry has its own timer; idle revocation is checked by the 15-second heartbeat. A boundary remains: once the SSE handler has passed checkSession and entered write(), logout does not cancel that write; ResponseWriter.Write/Flush is bounded by a 20-second deadline (internal/panel/terminal_stream.go:201-227). The docs contract read at terminal-file-transport-v3.md:210-212,238 sets one-second output rechecks, idle heartbeat cleanup, expiry close, a 20-second write timeout, and says transport-written bytes cannot be recalled. It does not settle whether an in-progress blocked event completing after logout success is acceptable or what a browser/proxy receives. The docs line 70 is the terminal input/PTY dispatch contract; I did not apply it to output SSE or to file relay. File relay is a distinct transport and no SSE revocation conclusion is made about it.

local_checks.invariant: After panel logout invalidates the browser session, the terminal SSE channel should stop delivering queued terminal output according to its documented recheck contract.
local_checks.result: Logout synchronously deletes the hashed session record; subsequent Authenticate fails when SessionByTokenHash cannot find it (internal/panel/server.go:1055-1072; internal/auth/service.go:577-610; internal/store/store.go:704-736). The SSE stream is bound to the user ID and token hash (internal/panel/terminal_stream.go:170-195). However, checkSession returns true without a new Authenticate while now-lastAuth is less than the one-second auth interval, and the output event path immediately calls write after that cached result (terminal_stream.go:233-264). Thus a dequeued output event can pass on a recently successful cached check after the session has been deleted; a write already entered before logout also has a 20-second deadline and is not canceled by the logout handler (terminal_stream.go:201-224; server.go:1055-1072). Docs promise recheck no more than once per second, sending auth.expired and ending after detecting revocation, not writing queued output after a failed check, and say transport-written bytes cannot be recalled (docs/terminal-file-transport-v3.md:210-212,238). This source read does not establish what a TLS/proxy/browser client actually receives after the logout response, and the docs do not clearly define whether output authorized by the most recent successful check may complete during the stale-check/write-deadline window. I retain the source-grounded timing candidate as needs_validation pending owner decision and isolated delivery evidence; I do not claim atomic logout-versus-write exclusion. This conclusion is specific to terminal SSE and does not import terminal input or file-relay cancellation contracts. Supporting source-review record retained at C:/GitHub/_codex-tmp/windows-cf-audit-20261003/agents/windows_cf_audit/scratch/verify-u16-terminal-sse.json.

unresolved: Owner must clarify whether the documented one-second authentication cache permits already-queued SSE output to be written after logout succeeds but before a fresh authentication check; no strict atomic ordering guarantee appears in the docs.
The source does not prove whether ResponseWriter/TLS/proxy buffering allows an event blocked on Write to reach the browser after the logout response, or the concrete client-visible timing.
The source-only pass confirms the timing window but not transport/client delivery or owner acceptance; no target execution was permitted.
